summary.short: Dutch bill implementing the EU AI Act: designates national market-surveillance and notifying authorities, grants them supervisory and fining powers, creates an AI regulatory sandbox, and amends sector laws. Entry into force is not yet set.
summary.long: Bill implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) in Dutch law. Article 2 names the Minister of Economic Affairs and Climate as notifying authority for certain AI systems, designates market-surveillance authorities by area (the AP, AFM, De Nederlandsche Bank and others), and sets the Minister as central contact point. Chapter 3 lets designated officials enter dwellings without consent after prior judicial authorisation, access AI systems under false identity details, impose self-standing orders on online intermediaries, and levy administrative fines up to the Article 99 AI Act amounts. Chapter 4 provides an AI regulatory sandbox and conditions on approved real-world testing. Chapter 5 sets cooperation and data-sharing rules between authorities. Article 7.1 requires providers of high-risk AI systems to keep documentation available to authorities after bankruptcy or cessation. Chapter 8 amends several sector laws (telecommunications, consumer goods, cable cars, medical devices, recreational craft, judiciary, financial supervision) with AI-specific authority, fine and language rules. Article 7.2 (registration of high-risk critical-infrastructure systems) and the entry-into-force date (Article 9.2) are marked PM.

notes: Bill text as introduced (voorstel van wet, KetenID WGK26950); no entry-into-force date: Art. 9.2 and Art. 7.2 (registration of high-risk AI systems in critical infrastructure) read PM. Amended-act rows are the bill's own amendments; target_instrument_id is empty because targets are not in the registry. Drafting issues: Art. 8.6(I) (Art. 14, fourth paragraph) reads het eerste elfde lid; Art. 8.3(A) lettering is garbled (onderdelen g tot en met j tot i tot en met l). Art. 9.1 is conditional on a proposed Wetboek van Strafvordering not yet enacted. Penalty amounts are only cross-referenced to Art. 99 of the AI Regulation.

thresholds.note: The bill contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Fine maxima (Art. 3.7, 8.3, 8.6, 8.9, 15.4, 18a, 29) are enforcement and are referenced to Art. 99 of the AI Regulation without amounts. The 14-day appeal period (Art. 3.2(3), 3.4(5)) is a procedural time limit and is an event, not a threshold. Art. 7.2 and Art. 9.2 (inwerkingtreding) are marked 'PM'. Scope terms such as 'AI-systeem met een hoog risico' are defined by reference to Art. 6(1) of the AI Regulation with no numeric value.
